_comment: Memorisation check on the HUMAN half of aicheck30.json (§11 D201), the method of §11 D200: each abstract cut to its first sentence, the model asked to continue it exactly as published, scored as word-5-gram recall against the TRUE continuation. Model: Ollama tag slm2-base = stock Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 Q4_K_M from rishibrucelee/gaply-slm-models. Direct /api/chat, NOT the product path, because the question is about the weights rather than about the classifier. 8 of 10 items scored: ac-h05 is a single-sentence abstract (no continuation to score) and ac-h09 is the journal front-matter fragment whose 21-word remainder is below the 30-word floor -- both skipped structurally, neither a failure. THE METRIC ITSELF WAS CONTROLLED before the zeros were believed: identical text scores 1.000, a true continuation against its own first half scores 0.476, unrelated text scores 0.000. Run on the BASE because memorisation is a property of the pretrained weights and slm2-tuned is those same weights plus a rank-32 LoRA; §11 D200 ran both, and this did not, which is the one place this check is narrower than the one it copies.

rows.first_sentence: This paper investigates consumer inertia in health insurance markets, where adverse selection is a potential concern.
rows.reply:
We consider a model of sequential decision making with two types of consumers: healthy and sick. The healthy consumers have a low probability of becoming sick, while the sick consumers have a high probability of remaining sick. Consumers are risk-averse and have a constant relative risk aversion (CRRA) utility function. They can purchase health insurance from an insurer or go without it.

rows.first_sentence: Document level sentiment classification remains a challenge: encoding the intrin-sic relations between sentences in the se-mantic meaning of a document.
rows.reply:
The proposed model is trained using a combination of supervised and unsupervised learning techniques. In the supervised learning phase, we use labeled data to train the sentence-level sentiment classifier. In the unsupervised learning phase, we use document embeddings to learn a representation of the overall sentiment of a document. This allows us to capture the intrinsic relations between sentences in the semantic meaning of a document.
